newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to announce private sector jail builders.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to announce private sector jail builders.

text.p: South Africa's public works ministry said on Monday that a shortlist of 11 private sector groups, bidding to build four multi-billion rand prisons with government financial backing, will be announced within the next two weeks.

The country, grappling with a spiralling crime wave and overcrowded jails, in May called for companies to bid for the design, construction, operation and maintenance of new penal facilities in four provinces.

Zaid Nordien, the ministry's public relations director told Reuters that 90 applications had been received but that these had been whittled down to 11 using criteria including the emphasis of black empowerment in each bid.

Minister Jeff Radebe said in a statement that the public-private sector partnership, the largest South Africa has seen so far, would promote emerging black contractors and entrepreneurs in the white-dominated building industry.

"(The project) is an important element in government's leverage to restructure the construction and property industries which to a large extent remain the monopoly of established white business," he said.

The successful companies will build two maximum-security jails each for 1,500 prisoners in the Northern Province and Free State, a similar-sized facility for awaiting trial prisoners in Gauteng and a further unit for 800 youth offenders in Mpumalanga.
The government-business venture follows the examples in the United States, Britain and Australia. A South African government delegation is currently in Britain to inspect facilities there.
Many of South Africa's existing prisons are severely run-down and overcrowded. The prison population has risen from 125,000 at the end of 1996 to over 130,000 at present.

Although political violence has dropped since president Mandela won the country's first all-race elections in 1994 criminal violence has soared. Police figures show 1.8 million crimes were reported in South Africa last year.
